description: Read by verify_claim_support.py. negation_words: whole words that negate (en, pt). negation_chars: Han characters that negate (zh). exceptions: phrases or Han compounds that contain a negation marker but do not negate; they are ignored before negation is detected. pt_markers: words found in Portuguese text but not in English; a text with one of them in lowercase is read as Portuguese, and so is a text with one capitalized at the start of a sentence ('O museu'), unless the next word is capitalized and the text contains an en_markers word ('Uma Thurman received an award'); if the next word is capitalized and the text has no en_markers word, the marker counts only if the text it is compared with reads as Portuguese on its own ('O Brasil fica no centro.' against 'O Brasil nunca fica no centro.'). pt_letters: accented letters found in Portuguese words but rarely in English loanwords; in a text without a pt marker, a clause with a lowercase word holding one of them ('histórico') is read as Portuguese, unless the text contains an en_markers word. en_markers: words found in English text but not in Portuguese, matched in any case; in a text that opens a sentence with a capitalized pt marker ('O Globo'), one counts only in lowercase or at the start of a sentence, since elsewhere a capitalized word is a name ('The Mall'). en_marker_exceptions: phrases used in Portuguese text that contain an en_markers word ('on-line', 'in loco', 'per capita'); in a text that opens a sentence with a capitalized pt marker, they are ignored before en_markers words are matched. pt_contractions: negation words that, in a text read as Portuguese, are contractions and do not negate ('no' = em + o). clause_separators: words (en, pt) that start a new clause, like a comma does; a negation counts only in a clause that carries the claim's content. antonyms: pairs of word-form lists with opposite meanings; a negated word equals its antonym, so 'not closed' matches 'open'. List every inflected form, since words are compared exactly. Matching is case-insensitive.
